content.text:
Fixed by making the runtime match the declared type rather than loosening the typings.

**Root cause** (`lib/reply.js:1001`): `onResponseCallback` forwarded `err` straight through to `LogController#requestCompleted`, and both paths that reach it produce `undefined` on success — the `reply.raw.on('finish', onResFinished)` listener invokes `onResFinished` with no argument, and `hookRunnerGenerator`'s `next()`/`handleResolve()` in `lib/hooks.js:230` calls `cb(err, …)` with `err` unset once all `onResponse` hooks pass. Meanwhile `types/logger.d.ts:127`, the JSDoc in `lib/log-controller.js:62`, and `docs/Reference/Server.md:522` all document `Error | null`.

**Change**: normalize with `err ?? null` at the single call site, so custom `LogController` subclasses that do `error === null` checks (as the docs imply) behave correctly. `types/logger.d.ts`, `lib/log-controller.js` and the docs were already correct and needed no change.

**Test**: added `requestCompleted receives null instead of undefined on a successful request` to `test/internals/logger.test.js`, which installs a `LogController` subclass and asserts the received `error` is strictly `null`. The test needs a `logger` option, since `lib/route.js:549` only calls `setupResponseListeners` when `hasLogger`, an `onResponse` hook, or a handler timeout is present.

`node --test test/internals/logger.test.js` → 34 pass, 0 fail. I also confirmed end-to-end via a throwaway script (since removed) that a custom controller now receives `null`.

Note on COMPLEX.md: `lib/reply.js` is listed under `hotspots`, but this COMPLEX.md contains only the frontmatter data — there is no "Why these files are hot" prose section, and no `load_bearing`, `seams`, or "What to read first" sections. `lib/reply.js` and `types/logger.d.ts` appear in no `co_change` pair, so there was no partner file to check.
